steps.what: Tend and observe equipment and machinery to verify efficient and safe operation

tasks.design: Keep direct equipment observation and tending with the helper under existing instructions. An existing {OPS_SYSTEM} maintenance record may receive concerns, with no sensor or autonomous safety function introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Safe operation needs observation of actual conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: No new technology is required for the retained work.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising conditions that require stopping and escalation.
tasks.human_edge: Notice abnormal behaviour and alert the responsible technician.
tasks.altitude: Observation and tending time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Maintenance record software does not establish replacement of the helper's physical observation and tending; this work remains.

assumptions: Boundary is helper observation and tending, excluding diagnosis, repair and the technician's response.
Helper produces observations directly in the fully retained step; no structured fault flag or reliable sensor feed is assumed.
No new system configuration or incremental upkeep.

steps.what: Check inventory and identify the new parts and quantities needed
Order new parts from approved catalogue items and confirm the order details

tasks.design: Configure native {PROCUREMENT} saved requests and catalogue orders linked to checked {OPS_SYSTEM} inventory requirements. The helper verifies item identity, quantity, delivery and price before sending within existing authority; unknown parts go to the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recurring parts orders may require repeated supplier and item entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Catalogue-based requests can reuse approved item identifiers and supplier details.
tasks.still_hard: A similar-looking part may be incompatible and inventory may be inaccurate.
tasks.human_edge: Check actual stock and seek technical confirmation when identity is uncertain.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated order entry, with stock and compatibility checks retained.

evidence.claim: Native catalogue requests can reduce repeated ordering entry; no helper-specific labour result is established in this digest.

assumptions: Boundary is helper stock checking and authorised ordering, excluding technician specification decisions, supervisor approval outside delegated limits and supplier fulfilment.

Helper produces item identifier, checked physical quantity, required order quantity, need date and delivery location during s1's full50 hours. Missing identifiers require technician confirmation, never a guessed catalogue match.
Technician maintains approved part specifications and buyer maintains existing supplier catalogue and limits; their ordinary capture remains unchanged. Extra mapping correction is counted below.
Order capture, price and compatibility checks remain25 hours in s2. Orders outside delegated authority follow existing approval procedures without claimed reduction.
Test native saved requests before code. Existing catalogue runtime earns no saving.
unknowns: Catalogue coverage and physical stock accuracy
research_questions: Does native request reuse save time after all identity checks and ordering exceptions?
